text:
This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all
preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of
craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.
plain: This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely, everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.
note: ESSAY 0 on screen: compressed answer (stack: verbatim over plain-english)

text: "Those wise ones get extinguished even like this lamp."

say: "What is burning?". "Those wise ones get extinguished even like this lamp."

text: "To project Nibbana into a distance and to hope that craving will be destroyed only on seeing it, is something like trying to build a staircase to a palace one cannot yet see."
"To think that the destruction of craving is not sufficient is like trying to give water to one who has already quenched his thirst."

say: "To project Nibbana — out, like a flame with no fuel — into a distance and to hope that craving will be destroyed only on seeing it, is something like trying to build a staircase to a palace one cannot yet see.". "To think that the wanting ends is not sufficient is like trying to give water to one who has already quenched his wanting."

text:
That form by which one designating the Tathagata might designate him,
that has been abandoned by him, cut off at the root, made like an
uprooted palm tree. The Tathagata is free from reckoning in terms of
form, deep, immeasurable and hard to fathom, like the great ocean.

say: That form by which one designating the Tathagata might designate him, that has been abandoned by him, cut off at the root, made like an uprooted palm tree. The Tathagata is past all counting in terms of form, so deep you cannot measure it, like the great ocean.

text:
It can in no way be compared to the extinction
  and the cooling down of the Arahants.

say: It can in no way be compared to going out, like a flame with no fuel and the cooling down of the Arahants.

text: "What is the use of a well, if water is there all the time, having cut craving at the root, in search of what should one wander?"

say: "What is the use of a well, if water is there all the time, having cut craving at the root, in search of what should one wander?"

text:
One who has quenched his thirst for good is aware of that blissful
  experience. When he sees the world running here and there in search
  of water, he looks within and sees the well-spring of his bliss.

say: One who has quenched his wanting for good is aware of that blissful experience. When he sees the world running here and there in search of water, he looks within and sees the well-spring of his bliss.

text:
This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all
preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of
craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.

say: This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely, everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.

text:
Sa-upadisesa: the arahant is free from fresh graspings, lust, hate
and delusions do not flare up. But so long as he has to bear the burden
of this organic combination, the arahant has to experience certain
afflictions.

say: the arahant is free from fresh holding on, lust, hate and delusions do not flare up. But so long as he has to bear the burden of this organic combination, the arahant has to experience certain afflictions.

text:
When he feels a feeling limited to the body, he understands 'I feel
a feeling limited to the body'... he understands 'on the breaking up
of this body, before life becomes extinct, even here itself, all that
is felt, not being delighted in, will become cool'.

say: When he feels a pleasant-or-unpleasant tone limited to the body, he understands 'I feel a pleasant-or-unpleasant tone limited to the body'... he understands 'on the breaking up of this body, before life becomes extinct, even here itself, all that is felt, not being delighted in, will become cool'.

text: Samsara or reiterated existence is itself a debt, which one can never pay off. When one comes to think of kamma and its result, it is a debt that keeps on gathering an interminable interest.
Even from this debt the arahants have won freedom by destroying the seeds of kamma, by rendering them infertile.

say: Samsara or reiterated existence is itself a debt, which one can never pay off. When one comes to think of kamma — what you do and what comes back — and its result, it is a debt that keeps on gathering an interminable interest.. Even from this debt the arahants have won freedom by destroying the seeds of kamma — what you do and what comes back —, by rendering them infertile.
